subject: Third‑party IP claim — mitigation options, redlines, and legal owners
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacorp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marco@procure.novacorp.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Third‑party notice we just received — request for next steps

Kim, Ben —

We just received a third‑party patent infringement letter related to a generated output allegedly containing a snippet from a third‑party model. Attached is the claim notice (PDF). Procurement asked me to loop you in immediately — they say the MSA/order form points to Redwood indemnity for third‑party IP claims.

What we need from you today:
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will defend or reimburse under the current draft language
- A list of evidence/proof you will need from Novacorp if we invoke the notice (we're preserving mailboxes, logs, etc.)
- Estimated timing for an initial written response to the claimant (they expect reply within 14 days)

This is time‑sensitive. Marco is on copy for procurement coordination.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: novacorp_claim_notice.pdf

--
Elena Ruiz
Sr. Contracts Manager, Novacorp Systems
elena.ruiz@novacorp.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacorp.com>, Marco Salazar <marco@procure.novacorp.com>, Outside Counsel <gc@lawfirmllp.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Third‑party notice we just received — request for next steps

Forwarding Novacorp's notice — tagging Ben and Jonas for legal / commercial input. Immediate thoughts:

1) We should avoid a blanket defend obligation across all customer outputs. Propose to limit to claims arising from (a) Customer‑uploaded proprietary training data and (b) Customer‑provided prompts that include third‑party copyrighted material.

2) Request a right‑to‑defend with mandatory cooperation and a narrow set of tactical exceptions (e.g., Customer may not unilaterally settle). If Novacorp insists on "defend and control," we need insurance/indemnity cap and a clear evidence preservation checklist.

3) Evidence: we will need original claimant notice, customer prompt/log slice, timestamped request IDs, and any downstream derivative claims. Suggest attaching a one‑page checklist to the order form so procurement knows what's required.

I've uploaded a fresh redline of the order form with these options: rdw_orderform_redline_v2.docx (attached). Please review and call out the following by EOD: recommended position (defend vs reimburse), proposed cap language, and whether we can require customer to cover outside counsel costs if they reject our reasonable defense strategy.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Lead Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacorp.com>, Marco Salazar <marco@procure.novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Third‑party notice we just received — request for next steps

Thanks Kim — quick commercial perspective from sales/procurement: Novacorp will push hard on broad defend language (they want minimal operational friction). We have some leverage on price and a short renewal coming up (Q1).

Suggested negotiation posture to start customer conversation:
- Offer Right‑to‑Defend as primary, but with a capped exposure (e.g., $5M aggregate per claim) and clear proof obligations.
- If customer demands defend & control, propose an insurance offset (their first party insurance pays down our exposure) and an incremental monthly fee for carrying the risk (we should ask for a 10–15% uplift to the order form).
- Add explicit exclusions for claims arising from (i) Customer modifications of our SDKs, (ii) Customer republishing other parties' content into prompts, and (iii) open‑source model components where third‑party licenses are implicated.

Next steps: legal crafts two short alternate clauses (A: right‑to‑defend w/ cap; B: defend & control w/ insurance + fee). I'll align with procurement to flag commercial concession grid and expected approval ladder.

Ben

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacorp.com>, Outside Counsel <gc@lawfirmllp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Third‑party notice we just received — legal recommendations

Appended legal guidance based on the claim and current order form draft. Key recommendations:

- Default stance: preserve a Right‑to‑Defend with control limited to Redwood where the alleged infringement arises from Redwood‑hosted model behavior and not from Customer‑supplied content. That preserves our ability to manage litigation strategy (cost and settlement discipline).

- If we must concede "defend & control": insist on (i) an express indemnity cap tied to order value/insurance, (ii) customer cooperation and explicit no‑settlement without us, and (iii) costs for compliance with evidence preservation if they fail to produce logs timely.

- Evidence & notice mechanics: require notice in writing to legal@redwood.com; require Customer to provide (a) claimant notice, (b) request IDs and raw logs for the implicated time window, (c) sample prompts and generated outputs, and (d) any license evidence (for third‑party content). Allow Redwood 30 days to investigate before any refund/settlement payment is due (to align with our incident review process).

- Tactical playbook: attach indemnity_evidence_checklist.xlsx to order form as an appendix; include a 60‑day document preservation requirement; require Customer to escrow disputed outputs when requested. These are reasonable asks for procurement to operationalize.

I'll prepare two short clause alternatives and mark the redline with comments on settlement and cost allocation. If Outside Counsel thinks client jurisdiction or narrow patent claims change the approach, we'll adapt, but the above gives us a strong starting position.

Jonas
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Ben will prepare a commercial concession grid and proposed pricing uplift for the broader defend approach.
